verses.42:1: Julgai-me, Deus, e {discerne} a minha causa {gente}, * arrancai-me do homem iníquo e enganador.
verses.42:2: Porque vós sois, Deus, a minha força: * por que me {repulisti}? e por que ando triste, {dum}?
verses.42:3: Enviai a vossa luz e a vossa verdade: * elas me {deduxerunt}, e me {adduxerunt} ao vosso monte santo, e {tabernacula}.
verses.42:4: E {introibo1} o altar de Deus: * {introibo2} o Deus que alegra a minha juventude.
verses.42:5: Eu vos darei graças com a cítara, Deus, meu Deus: * por que estás triste, {anima}? e por que me perturbas?
verses.42:6: Espera em Deus, porque ainda lhe darei graças: * {salutare}.

decisions.why: discérnere is to set apart, divide off (L&S), and here, with *de gente*, to decide the case by separating it (DRB 'distinguish my cause from'; MS1932 *separa a minha causa*; the Greek δίκασον τὴν δίκην is 'plead / judge my case'). The cognate *discerni* and DRB's *distingui* are both bare *vós* imperatives of -ir verbs that equal the first-person past ('I discerned', 'I distinguished') — rule 3 bans them. *Separai* is an -ar verb, safe, and keeps the Latin's picture of the one case taken out from the other.

options.label: discerni
options.note: the cognate; refused on the same ban.

options.label: defendei
options.note: the Greek and Hebrew 'plead my cause'; not the Latin's picture of separating.

decisions.why: gens → *nação* (gentes → nações, glossary; 32:12 *Beáta gens* → *Bem-aventurada a nação*); ἔθνους; DRB 'the nation that is not holy'. The cognate *gente* is barred by the ear: in Brazil *da gente* is 'from us' — *separai a minha causa da gente* would be heard as 'separate my cause from ours'. sanctus → *santo* (ὅσιος; glossary), the Latin's litotes *non sancta* kept rather than resolved to *ímpia* (DM1962, from the Hebrew). The Latin has no article; Portuguese needs one, and the indefinite keeps it as open as *de gente* (MS1932 *duma gente*).

options.label: da nação não santa
options.note: DRB's article; makes one nation definite, which the Latin does not.

options.label: de uma gente não santa
options.note: MS1932; the cognate; *gente* in Brazil is 'people, folks' or 'we'.

decisions.why: repéllere without *a* (ἀπωθέω, 'thrust away, cast off'); the glossary's *afastar* is for amovére / repéllere *a* (and 42:2 is named there as not settled by it); *rejeitar* is reprobáre's (117:22). The cognate *repelir* is plain, is MS1932's, and is free. 43:10, 59:3, 59:12, 73:1, 77:60, 77:67, 87:15, 88:39, 107:12 have the same verb (grep); proposed as a row. A -ir verb, but here it is a past (*repelistes*), not an imperative.

options.label: afastastes
options.note: the repéllere *a* row's verb; weaker than a thrust.

decisions.why: The Latin puts the enemy last. Portuguese allows it after *enquanto* (MS1932 *enquanto me aflige o inimigo*), but it is the literary order; the natural one ends on *aflige*, a paroxytone, as the Latin's *inimícus*. Order is the ear's (D2). The same clause closes 41:10 (with *contristátus*), which should read the same.

The Latin has perfects, as the Greek has aorists (ὡδήγησαν … ἤγαγον); DRB 'they have conducted me, and brought me'. MS1932 turns them to futures (*me conduzirão e me levarão*), the Hebrew's sense (jussive/imperfect) — not taken (rule 1): the Latin prays 'send them forth' because they have already led. dedúcere → *guiar* (D22; the row names 42:3). *ipsa* (neuter plural, light and truth) → *elas*.

options.label: guiaram
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's tense, D22's verb.

options.label: guiarão
options.note: MS1932's future (the Hebrew's sense); refused, rule 1.

decisions.latin: et adduxérunt in montem sanctum tuum
decisions.why: addúcere, 'lead to, bring to'. *levar* is the plainer of two faithful verbs and is MS1932's word for this verb; *conduzir* (the dedúci in row) is heavier and in this verse would sit beside *guiar* as its near-synonym. Once in the psalter (grep).

options.label: trouxeram
options.note: DRB 'brought'; puts the speaker already on the mountain.

decisions.why: tabernáculum → *tenda* (row, open; applied to God's tent at 14:1, 26:5, 30:21b); the plural is the Latin's (τὰ σκηνώματά). In this verse, said at the foot of the altar, a Brazilian ear may miss *tabernáculos* (MS1932), which in Brazil is the tabernacle of a church — the reason the row refused it.

decisions.latin: Et introíbo ad altáre Dei: * ad Deum, qui lætíficat
decisions.why: introíre → *entrar* (23:7 *introíbit Rex glóriæ* → *entrará*, 25:4 *non introíbo* → *não entrarei*); εἰσελεύσομαι πρός, DRB 'I will go in to the altar of God: to God who…'. The Latin repeats *ad … ad*; the second colon hangs on the first. Portuguese *entrar* takes *em*, not *a*; *até* says 'in, as far as', and repeated keeps the Latin's *ad … ad*, so that the second colon still reads alone — as it must: the verse is the antiphon at the foot of the altar, split between priest (*Introíbo ad altáre Dei*) and server (*Ad Deum, qui lætíficat juventútem meam*) (Ordo.txt), and the antiphon of the Sexagesima Communion (Quadp2-0). MS1932 *me aproximarei do* changes the verb. *Subirei ao altar* may be what Portuguese hand-missals print for this line — **not verified**, and *subir* is another image (going up), not the Latin's going in; it is not offered as an option for that reason, only recorded.

options.label: entrarei ao … ao
options.note: the Latin's *ad* as *a*; *entrar a* is not Brazilian Portuguese for going into a place.

decisions.why: The refrain of Pss 41–42 (41:6, 41:11b, 42:5; one psalm in the Hebrew). The soul is addressed, a single addressee → *tu* (*estás*, *perturbas*, and 42:6 *Espera*). The Latin has no *o*: the glossary's working rule for the vocative is no *ó* unless the Latin has it. A vocative drops the article (*minha alma*, not *a minha alma*). MS1932 *minha alma*; DRB 'O my soul'. Proposed as a formula row for Ps 41, translated in parallel.

options.label: ó minha alma
options.note: DRB 'O my soul'; the *ó* is not in the Latin.

decisions.latin: salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus
decisions.why: A bare apposition to *illi* (= God): he is 'the salvation of my face, and my God' (σωτήριον τοῦ προσώπου μου ὁ θεός μου; DRB 'the salvation of my countenance, and my God'). salutáre → *salvação* (D6), vultus → *rosto* (glossary). MS1932 supplies a relative (*a ele que é a salvação do meu rosto*), which explains; the Latin's apposition is kept, since *lhe* two words before names him. *Deus meus* is not a vocative here (nominative in apposition), so *o meu Deus*, with the article.

options.label: a salvação do meu rosto, e o meu Deus

forms.salutare: a salvação do meu rosto, e o meu Deus

options.label: a ele, a salvação do meu rosto, e o meu Deus

forms.salutare: a ele, a salvação do meu rosto, e o meu Deus

options.note: the pronoun repeated so the apposition is heard; *a ele* is not in the Latin.

options.label: a ele que é a salvação do meu rosto, e o meu Deus

forms.salutare: a ele que é a salvação do meu rosto, e o meu Deus

choices.42:1: judicáre → *julgar*, bare (row; 5:11a *julgai-os, Deus*; 7:9b *Julgai-me, Senhor*); the vocative *Deus* without *ó*, as 5:11a and 21:21. *causa* keeps its own word (the judicáre row notes 42:1). éruere with a source → *arrancar* (row; 31:7, 36:40, 38:9); the verb moved first (natural order, D2), so that the first word of the second colon is the imperative. dolósus → *enganador* (row; 5:7b *o homem de sangue e enganador*), iníquus → *iníquo* (kept apart from *ímpio*). The Introit of Passion Sunday (Quad5-0) quotes the verse with *éripe me* and adds *quia tu es Deus meus et fortitúdo mea* — another wording; the psalm keeps its own.
choices.42:2: Quia tu es → *Porque vós sois* (30:4 *Porque vós sois a minha força*). fortitúdo → *força* (row; 17:2, 30:4, 117:14). quare → *por que* (2:1, 21:2). incédere → *andar* (37:7 *contristátus ingrediébar* → *eu andava entristecido*); tristis → *triste*, kept apart from 41:10's *contristátus* (→ *entristecido*, as 34:14, 37:7), which otherwise has the same second colon. afflígere → *afligir* (row).
choices.42:3: emíttere → *enviar* (MS1932 *Envia*; DRB 'send forth'); the Transfiguration versicle (Sancti/08-06) quotes the first colon alone, and Passion Sunday's Gradual and Quad5-2's the whole — it reads alone. véritas → *verdade* (row). mons sanctus → *monte santo*, adjective after (row; 14:1 *no vosso monte santo*).
choices.42:4: lætificáre → *alegrar* (row, open; 18:9, 29:2). juvéntus → *juventude* (24:7 *Das faltas da minha juventude*). Corpus Christi's antiphon (horas Pent01-4) adapts the verse (*sumam Christum, qui rénovat juventútem meam*) — not the psalm's wording.
choices.42:5: confitéri → *dar graças* (D5); *Confitébor tibi* → *Eu vos darei graças* (9:2, 34:18, 117:21). cíthara → *cítara* (row; 32:2). *Deus, Deus meus* → *Deus, meu Deus* (21:2 formula). conturbáre → *perturbar* (row). The second colon is the refrain of Ps 41 (41:6, 41:11b) — see decision `anima` and the glossary formula row.
choices.42:6: = 41:6 (second line) and 41:12, word for word; Ps 41 should copy it. *Spera* (to the soul, *tu*) → *Espera em* (speráre in → *esperar em*, D36; 36:3 *Espera no Senhor*). adhuc → *ainda*. *confitébor illi* → *lhe darei graças* (27:7b *lhe darei graças*).

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm42.txt, 6 prayed verses (42:1–42:6; no titulus, D7). One mediant per verse, no flex. Uses by grep (ps032/uses.py): the whole psalm is said at the foot of the altar in the traditional Mass, verse by verse alternately between priest and server, with the antiphon *Introíbo ad altáre Dei. — Ad Deum, qui lætíficat juventútem meam* split at the mediant of 42:4 (missa Ordo.txt, Ordo67, OrdoA, OrdoS, Holy Saturday Quad6-6); Passion Sunday Introit and Gradual (Quad5-0, with *éripe me* and an added *Deus meus*), Quad5-2 gradual verse, Sexagesima Communion (Quadp2-0: 42:4 whole), Transfiguration versicle (horas Sancti/08-06: 42:3a), Corpus Christi antiphon (horas Pent01-4, adapted). So every colon must read alone. Pss 41 and 42 are one psalm in the Hebrew (Heb 42–43): 42:5b = 41:6a = 41:11b; 42:6 = 41:6b = 41:12; 42:2b is 41:10b with *tristis* for *contristátus*. Ps 41 had no prayed.json when this draft was made, so the refrain is proposed here as a glossary formula row.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps042.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Formulas checked with ps038/xref.py and ps005/grep_latin.py. Rulings applied: D5 (confitéri → dar graças, twice), D6 (salutáre), D22 (dedúcere → guiar, the row names 42:3), D36 (speráre in → esperar em), D19 not met. Rows applied: judicáre, éruere (with a source → arrancar), dolósus, fortitúdo, afflígere, tabernáculum → tenda, mons sanctus, lætificáre, cíthara, conturbáre, vultus. Latin kept against the Hebrew/MS1932: 42:3 perfects *guiaram … levaram* (MS1932 futures). Rule 3 decided 42:1 *separai* (*distingui*, *discerni* are 'I distinguished / discerned'). Tests for the readers: *de uma nação não santa*, *me repelistes*, *às vossas tendas*, *entrarei até o altar … até o Deus*, *a salvação do meu rosto, e o meu Deus*, the refrain's *minha alma*.

Draft 1: hard pass. Length: 42:2 second colon +3 (two questions and a clause; *enquanto* for *dum*), 42:3 second −3; accepted. No rhyme flags. Cadences: oxytone finals where the Latin is paroxytone at 42:4a (*Deus*), 42:5a (*meu Deus*), 42:6b (*o meu Deus*) — the Latin's own word at the cadence; allowed by rule 4.
